messages:
perf-bot: ALERT p99 hosted-api > 1.2s for model-g-1 across us-west-2 (10:02:03)
Alex B.: seeing it on the dashboards now — p95 ~420ms but p99 jumped to 1.6s around 09:58 UTC :eyes:
Priya K.: is this related to the midnight rollout for model-g-1 quantized variant? any version pin changes?
Sam W.: no rollout on hosted side yesterday. infra reports a spike in queue depth on pool-gpu-3 at ~09:56
infra-bot: pool-gpu-3: queue_depth=128, in_flight=32, avg_batch_size=2.1, evictions=43m, cpu_steal=12%
Alex B.: interesting, avg_batch_size dropped from 6 -> 2.1 which would increase per-token overhead. Could be batching heuristic fallback.
Marcus L.: checked kernel selection logs on host-3: a bunch of select_kernel() fallbacks to generic_matmul int8 path after kernel cache misses
Sam W.: paste of profiler (summarized):
```
hot functions:
  select_kernel()   45%  (cache_miss paths)
  kv_cache_get()    22%
  batch_assembler() 15%
  sync_wait()       10%
```
Priya K.: KV cache evictions 43m from infra-bot — sounds like noisy neighbor thrashing memory and evicting KV shards. Any node-level OOMs or K8s evictions? :thinking:
infra-bot: no OOMs. dmesg shows frequent PCI errors on host-3 around 09:55 (recovered). GPU driver driver-reset=1 events
Alex B.: PCI resets can flush kernel-level caches -> cause kernel selection to recompile and drop optimized kernels. That explains select_kernel churn.
Sam W.: also saw burst of small requests from a single api-key  -- rate ~600rps for short window, generated tiny batch sizes. Could be a bad client or test job.
Marcus L.: query logs: api-key xxxxx triggered 18k requests in 3m starting 09:54, most with short prompts (<30 tokens)
Priya K.: so combined: noisy client causing small batches + host PCI resets leading to kernel cache miss -> select slower kernel + KV thrash due to memory pressure -> p99 spike. Good hypothesis.
Alex B.: mitigation options: 1) throttle offending api-key 2) force warm kernels (precompile) on pool-gpu-3 3) increase KV cache capacity / pin critical shards
Sam W.: I'm going to throttle that api-key for now (rate-limit 50rps) and add a temporary route to divert to pool-gpu-5
Sam W.: done — applied quota and rerouted ~09:59 :white_check_mark:
perf-bot: METRIC p99 dropped to 0.48s within 90s of throttling
Marcus L.: starting kernel warm job on pool-gpu-3 to prepopulate kernel cache and fill KV cache for hot model variants
Priya K.: can we add a heuristic: if avg_batch_size < 3 and model small -> combine into bigger synthetic batches? might mitigate small-request bursts
Alex B.: note: synthetic batching has latency SLO tradeoffs but worth an experiment for tiny prompts. I'll file an RFC after this incident.
Sam W.: postmortem action items (quick):
- block / throttle abusive api-key temporarily (completed)
- add kernel warm job to startup hooks for pools (in progress)
- add alert for sudden avg_batch_size drop + queue_depth rise
- investigate PCI reset root cause with cloud provider
Marcus L.: logging the thread in incidents channel and will start a short postmortem doc
Alex B.: thanks everyone — monitoring closely, will update if anything else pops up :thumbsup:
